candidate: IV-4 p. 324, proof of (21.14.1): 'tout idéal premier q de B non contenu dans p est principal'
print: Tout revient évidemment à prouver que tout idéal premier 𝔮 de B non contenu dans 𝔭 est principal. (run_IV4/page_324_s1.png)
correct: tout idéal premier $\mathfrak q$ de $B$ de hauteur $1$ non contenu dans $\mathfrak p$ est principal
argument: A 1-codimensional cycle on Spec(B) is a combination of height-1 primes; if Z is principal at 𝔭, Z − div(f) involves only height-1 primes 𝔮 ⊄ 𝔭, so the theorem reduces to: every height-1 prime 𝔮 ⊄ 𝔭 is principal. The proof proves exactly that: it uses that 𝔮 is divisorial (𝔮D_0 divisorial by Bourbaki AC VII §1 no 10 prop 15) and that 𝔮_1 = 𝔮∩A[T] is a prime of height 1. Without the qualifier the claim is false: for A a complete DVR and B = A[[T]] (hypotheses hold, dim B = 2 > 1), the maximal ideal (π, T) is prime, not contained in 𝔭 = πB, and not principal. 'de hauteur 1' was dropped; the English ('of height one') and the Spanish ('de altura 1', with a footnote) already have it.
